annotation.title_clean: ASME 2026 Competition: Waste-Sorting Robot; Ethical Modeling for Autonomous Vehicle Decision Making and its Societal Implications
annotation.title_en: ASME 2026 Competition: Waste-Sorting Robot; Ethical Modeling for Autonomous Vehicle Decision Making and its Societal Implications
annotation.venue: University of Virginia Libra Online Archive (School of Engineering and Applied Science)
annotation.summary_en: Undergraduate thesis portfolio from the University of Virginia combining an ASME student competition waste-collection robot capstone with an STS paper on how autonomous vehicle AI should make ethical decisions in unavoidable accidents. It argues for a law-based rather than utilitarian framework, citing accountability, feasibility and transparency. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Argues AVs should use a law-based ethical framework rather than a utilitarian one in unavoidable accidents
Evaluates frameworks on technical feasibility, ethical fairness and public transparency
Law-based systems give clearer accountability and are easier to define and implement
Compares AVs with human drivers using crash data, legal outcomes and labor market impacts
Capstone designs a waste collection robot complying with ASME competition rules and safety requirements
